title: transfer.sh
same: Every counted sample's results were read from its own job logs. In all 15 cold samples (5 per configuration) the same 25 checks ran and passed: `go vet` and the tests of the `cmd`, `server` and `server/storage` packages under Go 1.26, Go 1.27 and Go tip, golangci-lint, and the Go binary, the image and the `noroot` image for each of linux/386, linux/amd64, linux/arm/v7 and linux/arm64. The root package has no test files in any run. In the 15 warm samples the same 25 checks passed, but Go took some package test results from its test cache instead of re-running them, in every configuration alike: the three Go 1.26 packages in every warm sample, and the three Go 1.27 packages as well in 4 of the 15 (1 GitHub, 1 StarSling unchanged, 2 StarSling + agent PR). Go tip's tests were never reused. Each reused result is linked to the seed run that produced it (see How it's measured). The binaries were not compared byte for byte: with the agent PR, Go cross-compiles them with the same command and flags (CGO off, static) instead of compiling each one under emulation.
notes: **Workflows in this merge.** The replayed merge changes only `README.md`. Upstream's `test.yml` and `build-docker-images.yml` have no path filters, so both run on every merge to the default branch. `release.yml` runs only on a published release or a manual dispatch, so it does not run here (upstream's own run for it on this merge was a workflow-file error with no jobs).

**Bench-only changes, identical in every configuration (GitHub, StarSling unchanged, StarSling + agent PR) and never part of the agent PR:**
  - Switched off: the Docker Hub login, the image push step (`Docker Buildx (push)`), the manifest check and the `Clear` step. Upstream's own condition is kept with `false &&` in front. The registry secrets do not exist here and nothing may be published. Upstream did run these steps on this merge (the `Docker Buildx (push)` step builds both images again and publishes them), so that upstream work is not in any column.
  - The two secret references (`DOCKER_USERNAME`, `DOCKER_PASSWORD`) are removed; only the switched-off login step reads them.
  - Runner labels: upstream's `ubuntu-latest` is replaced by the runner label of each configuration (see Runner sizes).
  - One harness step, `Benchmark event context (harness)`, is added at the start of every job. It prints two IDs so each job can be matched to its sample; its median time is 0 s.
  - On the agent PR's own branch (`starsling/develop`) only, a setup commit points the two workflows' triggers at that branch and their runners at StarSling, so the PR's checks run there. The measured replays do not use it.

**Replaced samples.** One sample that never finished was discarded and re-run. It was the StarSling + agent PR sample of cold round 4; it left no record. The experiment was reopened (the reopening is recorded in `experiments/full-1`) and the sample re-run from a fresh cold cache. Separately, the StarSling + agent PR sample of cold round 3 failed at `actions/checkout` in two test jobs before any test ran, and was re-run; that is the 1 re-run sample counted below. In every counted sample, no job waited more than 19 s for a runner.

**Warm runs and reused test results.** Before each warm sample, a seed run replays the previous upstream merge ([`eae01b5b`](https://github.com/dutchcoders/transfer.sh/commit/eae01b5b953adb928ec804f66ac8b8fe6bbfb503), onto `c2f4a4cf`) on the same configuration; its time is not counted. Every Go test result a warm sample reused from Go's test cache (57 in all, across the 15 warm samples) is linked in the evidence record to the seed run that produced it, and that seed run passed: [`experiments/full-1/evidence/evidence.json`](https://github.com/starsling-demo-org/benchmark-transfer.sh/blob/bench/control/experiments/full-1/evidence/evidence.json) (for example, warm round 1 with the agent PR reused results from seed [run 43828737998](https://github.com/starsling-demo-org/benchmark-transfer.sh/actions/runs/43828737998)).

**Runner sizes.** Upstream's `ubuntu-latest` jobs run on GitHub `ubuntu-26.04-4core` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) and StarSling `starsling-ubuntu-26.04` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB). StarSling's 4 vCPU runners can burst to 5 vCPU and 32 GB RAM (Afterburner); GitHub's 4-core runners have 16 GB. Every job in this merge runs on those labels.

**Upstream reference (context only; not like-for-like; not the headline).** What upstream sees today: a median 25.5 min per merge to the default branch on upstream's own GitHub runners (n=12, most recent comparable merges to the default branch within the last 60 days; standard runners, warm caches, low commit rate; not a like-for-like replay).
**PR updates:** not measured. Both workflows also run on pull requests, but no upstream pull request was pinned for replay, so only the merge to the default branch was measured.

agentPrs.summary: Two changes in one PR. (A) The Dockerfile cross-compiles the Go binary for each target CPU instead of compiling it under CPU emulation; one file, the Dockerfile. (B) `test.yml` caches the Go tip toolchain, keyed on Go tip's latest commit, so it is built from source only when tip has moved.

whatWasSlow: Every merge to transfer.sh's default branch starts two workflows at once. `build-docker-images.yml` has one job, `buildx`, which builds the image twice (the normal image and a `noroot` variant), each for four platforms: linux/386, linux/amd64, linux/arm/v7 and linux/arm64. The Go compile ran once per platform inside that platform's container, so the ARM builds compiled under a CPU emulator. The first build runs with `--no-cache --pull`, so no cache can help it. That one job is almost the whole wait: in this benchmark, cold, it took a median 1168 s of the 1171 s merge on GitHub, and 456 s of the 464 s merge on StarSling runners before any change. Alongside it, `test.yml` runs the tests under Go 1.26, Go 1.27 and Go tip, plus golangci-lint. The Go tip job builds Go itself from source on every run: that install step took a median 184 s on GitHub and 70 s on StarSling runners, cold. It is not on the wait (the Docker job is longer), but it is runner time on every merge.
whatWeChanged:
The original showcase for this project proposed two fixes. Both are in one agent PR. The full benchmark measured them stacked together, and each fix was checked on the CI step it changes, on StarSling, with 5 runs on each side (the CI as it was, and the CI with the fix). Cold means no caches at the start; warm means starting from caches a seed run left behind.

| Fix | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| A. Cross-compile the Go binary instead of compiling it under CPU emulation | Image build step, cold: 442 s to 74 s (median), **6.0x faster**; every run with the fix beat every run without it. Warm: 439 s to 74 s | Kept (agent PR 1) |
| B. Cache the Go tip toolchain, keyed on Go tip's latest commit | Go tip test job, warm: 96 s to 40 s (median), **2.4x faster**; every run with the fix beat every run without it. Cold (nothing to restore): 102 s to 107 s, a few seconds slower for the cache lookup and save | Kept (agent PR 1) |

Fix A shortens the wait and the runner time. Fix B saves runner time only: the Go tip job runs alongside the longer Docker job. Fix B's gain depends on Go tip not having moved since the last cached run: in the warm runs the seed run had already cached the same tip commit; on a merge after tip has moved, the cache misses and the job runs as it does cold.

Because fix B uses a cache, the full benchmark runs both cold and warm. It compares GitHub-hosted runners, StarSling with the CI unchanged, and StarSling with the agent PR applied, over 5 rounds for each.
